figures.llm_description: Fig. 1 | The multiferroic family tree. Multiferroicity, arising from the combined interplay of magnetic and ferroelectric mechanisms, can result from several  different sources. Here, we outline different combinations of these ‘root’ mechanisms and how they are responsible for different types of multiferroic  materials. figures.title: Figure 3
figures.llm_description: Fig. 3 | The Bi2O3–Fe2O3 phase diagram. The shaded area indicates the  composition range that we expect to be most promising for discovering  previously unidentified multiferroics through detailed bulk and artificially  engineered thin-film synthesis. Searches for polytypoid structures with  different fractions of magnetic and polar components within this phase  diagram also offer a hitherto unexplored opportunity. Adapted from ref. 55, APS.
